title: fix(runtime): MCP list_actions marks a confirmation-gated action unavailable for an AI service account
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6JaoSLDKWQ8v7cxY9uDGijfncD)_

Fixes #33067

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:MCP `list_actions` 给 AI 服务账号列出声明了 `ai.requiresConfirmation: true` 的动作时,在该行标上 `unavailable`,带 `run_action` 实际会回的 428 代码与原句。
- 为什么改:服务账号永远不能替自己确认,`run_action` 每次都拒;但列表说它可用,无人值守的 agent 据此规划,注定失败。
- 风险与回滚:只多答一个标记,不新拒任何输入;真人、代理用户的 agent 与系统上下文的列表不变。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` 的 `listActions` 标记处(新增 confirmation 判定与 `??` 顺序);`packages/runtime/src/action-confirmation-gate.test.ts` 末尾新 describe。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run src/action-confirmation-gate.test.ts`,预期 18 passed。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

- `listActions` (`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`) now asks, for a caller `isAiServiceAccountCaller` is true of, the run door's own `actionConfirmationRefusal`, and marks the row `unavailable: { code, reason }` with that refusal's code (`ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`) and sentence ("… An AI service account does not confirm an action for itself: a person runs this action."). Both predicates were already exported; nothing in `action-execution.ts` / `action-dispatch.ts` changed and the rule is not restated.
- The marker follows the DECLARED `ai.requiresConfirmation` flag (the predicate reads `=== true` only), never `actionLooksDestructive`.
- Order: the run path asks the confirmation gate in the admission sequence (`action-dispatch.ts`, the CONFIRMATION GATE block before the subject load), and the forward-credential refusal only later, inside `forwardApiAction` in the dispatch arms. So where both apply the mark is the confirmation refusal (`confirmation ?? apiForwardCredentialRefusal(...)`).
- A person, a delegated agent (`onBehalfOf` set) and the system context are not asked the gate at all: their listing is byte-for-byte as before.
- `McpActionSummary.unavailable` JSDoc (`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`) named only the endpoint case and `UNAUTHENTICATED`; it now names the account case and its code. Surface note for the seat: this JSDoc is the exported description of when `unavailable` appears, the same family as the tool description the order lists; I read it as inside the "description" row. No other text changed.
- The `list_actions` tool description ("An action that carries "unavailable" cannot be run with the credential you connected with … unavailable.reason says why and what would let it run") stays true for a service-account key, so it is unchanged and no `Skills-docs:` line is owed. The served skill (`skill-md.ts` + Console mirror) does not mention `unavailable`.
- Stdio twin: `stdio-data-bridge.ts` implements no `listActions`; the stdio server registers `list_actions` through the same `registerActionTools` over whatever bridge the host passes, so there is no second listing to align.
- Ruling: ADR-0151 D3 rule 3, read at `docs/adr/0151-ai-service-account-a-headless-agent-is-a-registered-principal-of-its-own.md` line 74: "An action that asks for a person's confirmation before it runs (ADR-0011's `ai.requiresConfirmation`, rule 3's co-sign) is refused for an account, and never confirmed by the account itself". Ruling grep (`ruling|Ruling-ref|maintainer|⛔`) over the edited spans of `listActions`, `actionConfirmationRefusal` / `isAiServiceAccountCaller` and the `McpActionSummary.unavailable` JSDoc: 0 hits (file-wide: mcp.ts 17, action-execution.ts 65, mcp-http-tools.ts 39, none in or governing these spans).

## Tests

New top-level `describe` in `packages/runtime/src/action-confirmation-gate.test.ts` (the confirmation gate's shared harness), each case pairing the listing with `run_action` on the same bridge (`HttpDispatcher.buildMcpBridge`):

1. THE GAP: the account's gated row carries `unavailable` equal to `{ code, reason }` of the refusal; `run_action` with and without the confirmation member throws that exact code (428) and message; no handler ran and no record was read.
2. Declared flag, not heuristic: a `mode: 'delete'` row (listing still says `requiresConfirmation: true`), a declared-`false` danger row and a plain row stay bare for the account, and the destructive-looking one runs.
3. Both refusals: a gated identity-route `api` action under an API key: `run_action` answers `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` and the mark equals it. CONTROL: a person on the same key keeps the `UNAUTHENTICATED` forward-credential mark.
4. CONTROL: a person, a delegated agent and the system context see the gated row with no marker, and no row marked at all.

Measured first at `origin/main` (`dd4ce50b`, test commit `f6f2fa19` before the fix): cases 1 and 3 red: the gated row had no `unavailable` (`expected undefined to deeply equal { …(2) }`), and for the combined case the listing said `UNAUTHENTICATED` while `run_action` answered `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` (the run half of case 3 passed, so the 428 was measured).

<details><summary>Ablations (each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, anchor 1 → 0, restored to the HEAD blob, `git diff HEAD` empty)</summary>

- A, listing ignores the account rule (`const refusal = apiForwardCredentialRefusal(...)`): 2 failed / 16 passed (cases 1 and 3).
- B, the gate asked for every caller (`const confirmation = true ? …`): 2 failed / 16 passed (cases 3 and 4: the person and delegated agent get a marker).
- C, forward refusal first (`apiForwardCredentialRefusal(...) ?? confirmation`): 1 failed / 17 passed (case 3).

The suite imports `./http-dispatcher.js` from `src`, so no `dist/` rebuild sits between mutation and run.
</details>

## Acceptance notes

- `requiresConfirmation` on the row is still `actionLooksDestructive` (declared flag, else `mode: 'delete'` / `variant: 'danger'`); only the `unavailable` marker follows the declared flag. A row can therefore say `requiresConfirmation: true` with no marker for an account: that action runs for it (case 2 pins it).
- For an object-less action the reason's "on 'OBJECT'" clause reads the same declaration key `run_action` passes to the gate; not pinned separately here.
